mainEntity.name: Can functional medicine help hair loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We treat hair loss by addressing what is starving the follicle, thyroid, hormones, iron, and nutrients, rather than coating the strand. Most people see shedding slow and regrowth begin as the root causes are corrected.

mainEntity.name: What testing do you run for hair loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: We go beyond a basic panel, with full thyroid, iron and ferritin, hormones, and vitamin D, plus a scalp assessment, so the plan targets your specific root causes.

mainEntity.name: How long until I see new growth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hair grows slowly, so shedding usually settles first, within a couple of months, and visible regrowth follows over several. We track it with you.

mainEntity.name: Can stress and postpartum changes cause this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Both can push many follicles into shedding at once. We confirm the trigger and support your body so the cycle recovers.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer virtual hair loss care or only in person in Atlanta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. See Dr. Nina Ross in person at our Atlanta clinic, or virtually anywhere in Georgia. Your $99 Symptom Consultation can be booked either way.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: Root-cause hair loss care in Atlanta from a board-certified trichologist.

paragraphs: If your part is widening, your ponytail is thinner and the strands on the shower floor have you worried, you are not imagining it.

Your hair is telling you something about your health, and it deserves someone who will listen to the whole story. At Nina Ross Functional Medicine, we treat hair loss at its root, here in Atlanta and virtually across Georgia. Dr. Nina Ross is a board-certified trichologist who follows the whole picture, thyroid, hormones, and iron, until she finds what is really thinning your hair, then builds the plan around your body and your life.

sections.label: Why conventional care misses it

headings.text: You were told it is genetic, learn to live with it.

eyebrowSpans: Why conventional care keeps missing it
paragraphs: A fifteen-minute visit rarely has room to investigate why hair thins. So hair loss gets called genetic or stress, and the cause beneath it goes unexamined.

boldPairs.title: What you’re usually told
boldPairs.body: “It is probably just genetic. Try this shampoo and see how it goes.”

boldPairs.title: What’s actually happening
boldPairs.body: Hormones, thyroid, and nutrient gaps are starving the follicle in a loop. Address the loop and the follicle can recover.

sections.label: The functional medicine difference

headings.text: We will not hand you a shampoo and call it answered.

paragraphs: Here is where we part ways with conventional care. When hair thins, the reflex answer is a topical or the verdict that it is simply genetic. A product can coat the strand for a while. But nothing growing from a starved follicle holds, because the cause sits inside the body, in your hormones, thyroid, and nutrient stores, not on the surface of your scalp.
We would rather do the harder, more honest work. We find what is actually thinning your hair and we treat that.
If a topical or medication still has a place in your plan, that should be your informed choice, made with the full picture in front of you, not a default handed to you in a fifteen minute visit.

boldPairs.title: It treats the strand, not the follicle
boldPairs.body: A topical works on the surface while the follicle is being starved from within.

boldPairs.title: Genetic is rarely the whole story
boldPairs.body: Even with a genetic tendency, thyroid, iron, and hormones decide how much you actually lose.

boldPairs.title: It postpones the real regrowth
boldPairs.body: A follicle left starved eventually goes dormant, and the window to recover it narrows.

sections.label: The root-cause view

headings.text: Hair loss runs in a loop. We map the whole circle.

paragraphs: Each driver pushes the next. That is why treating one in isolation rarely holds, and why mapping the full cycle changes everything.
When we investigate your hair, we read the whole hormonal and nutritional picture rather than the scalp alone, and connect each driver back to what you’re seeing:

strongBullets.label: Thyroid function
strongBullets.full: Thyroid function, an under or overactive thyroid behind sudden, diffuse shedding.

strongBullets.label: Hormone shifts
strongBullets.full: Hormone shifts, where androgens, postpartum, and perimenopause thin the hair.

strongBullets.label: Low iron & ferritin
strongBullets.full: Low iron & ferritin, one of the most common and missed causes of hair loss.

strongBullets.label: Nutrient gaps
strongBullets.full: Nutrient gaps, vitamin D, zinc, and protein the follicle needs to grow.

strongBullets.label: Scalp inflammation
strongBullets.full: Scalp inflammation, a tender or flaky scalp that disrupts healthy growth.

strongBullets.label: Cortisol & stress
strongBullets.full: Cortisol & stress, that pushes follicles into shedding months later.

strongBullets.label: Blood sugar & insulin
strongBullets.full: Blood sugar & insulin, that influence the androgens affecting your hair.
